newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland seen in first group to join EMU - poll.
newsitem.headline: Finland seen in first group to join EMU - poll.

text.p: Operators on Finnish financial markets overwhelmingly think Finland will be in the first group of countries to join the third phase of European economic and monetary union (EMU) if it starts on time in 1999, according a Reuters poll.
Of 23 respondents (dealers, analysts and economists at banks and corporate treasury departments), 22 said they thought Finland would be among the first in the single currency.
The participants were asked "Do you believe that Finland will be among the first countries to join the third phase of EMU, if it starts according to plan on January 1, 1999?"
The poll was conducted by telephone on an anonymous basis on Thursday, February 27.

Participants: Aktia Bank, Bank of America (London), Banque Indosuez (Stockholm), CD Derivatives Ltd., Davy Protos, Den Danske Bank (Copenhagen), Enso, Handelsbanken Markets Finland, Huhtamaki Finance, I.D.E.A. (London), Interbank, IVO, Kemira, Kesko, Merita Bank, Neste, Nokia, OKOBANK, Postipankki, SE-Banken (Helsinki), SOK, Unibank (Copenhagen) and UPM-Kymmene.
